message.reasoning:
We need to answer question: "does SSO turning on kill password login instantly". The policy excerpts: DOC-009 part 1: enabling SSO does not immediately disable password sign-in for existing staff. Both methods coexist until an admin separately turns password sign-in off, in Settings → Security → SSO → Require SSO. Part 3: Once every staff member has confirmed they can sign in through SSO, enabling “Require SSO” turns off password sign-in for the whole workspace in one step.

Thus answer: No, enabling SSO alone doesn't kill password login; you need to enable Require SSO. Provide that info. Also mention that password sign-in remains until admin turns it off. So answer accordingly.

arguments.message: No – turning on SSO alone doesn’t immediately disable password sign‑in. Both methods stay available until an admin goes to Settings → Security → SSO and turns on “Require SSO.” Once that switch is enabled, password login is turned off for the whole workspace in one step.
